caption:
The water board asked by mail. Now ERCOT asks before the power flows.

Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 count 334 data center facilities. 233 never submitted a requested water use survey. The Tribune reports a fine of up to $500 for skipping it. The board says it has no authority of its own to prosecute.

Does ERCOT's request reach those 233? Its list is drawn differently. The survey goes only to operating data centers. The request reaches proposed ones of 25 to under 75 MW classed as Substantiated and Batch Zero facilities or additions not yet energized.

ERCOT's September 14th notice puts the water board's questions in Section C. A complete response carries a notarized attestation. A failure to respond is reported to the PUC and the Office of the Governor.

Will the report ERCOT expects to publish by December 10th say how many responded?

#ERCOT #TWDB #BatchZero

Sources

c21 Each transmission or distribution service provider files the RFI for the data center developer. https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/mkt_notices/M-B091426-01
c23 Any failure to respond will be reported to the PUC and the Office of the Governor. https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/mkt_notices/M-B091426-01

c26 ERCOT expects to publish that report by December 10th. https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/mkt_notices/M-B091426-01
c27 Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 identified 334 unique data center facilities. https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/14/texas-data-centers-water-use-penalties-enforcement/
c28 By the Tribune's count, 101 of those facilities submitted the survey at least once. https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/14/texas-data-centers-water-use-penalties-enforcement/
c29 The Tribune reported that 233 of those facilities never submitted a requested survey. https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/14/texas-data-centers-water-use-penalties-enforcement/

c35 State officials don't know whether any misdemeanor penalties have been issued against data centers. https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/14/texas-data-centers-water-use-penalties-enforcement/
c36 Raising Water Code fines for Class C misdemeanors would take state legislation. https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/14/texas-data-centers-water-use-penalties-enforcement/

c39 The survey is mailed to thousands of municipal public water systems and industrial facilities. https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/14/texas-data-centers-water-use-penalties-enforcement/
c40 The survey reaches only data centers that were operating in the year being surveyed. https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/14/texas-data-centers-water-use-penalties-enforcement/

document_title: 233 data centers never returned the water survey

slides.headline: Asked how much water they use, 233 never answered.
slides.dek: Records the Texas Tribune obtained for 2020 through 2025 count 334 data center facilities. Of those, 101 returned the water board's survey at least once. One bore for each facility, drawn to illustrate.

slides.headline: 101 answered, 233 never did
slides.dek: A brass plug seals the bore of each facility that returned a survey at least once. No bore stands for a named facility. The plate is drawn to illustrate.

slides.headline: Up to $500
slides.dek: Skipping the survey is a Class C misdemeanor, the Tribune reports. The water board says it has no authority of its own to prosecute. State officials don't know whether any misdemeanor penalty has been issued against a data center.

slides.headline: The survey's line is 10 million gallons a year
slides.dek: It goes to operating facilities using more than that, the Tribune reports. This tank holds that much, drawn to illustrate. The survey doesn't ask how a data center cools its servers.

slides.headline: 97 facilities reported 1.4 billion gallons
slides.dek: The Tribune reports the total from last year's survey. That much would fill 140 tanks of 10 million gallons, drawn here to illustrate.

slides.headline: Now the grid operator asks
slides.dek: ERCOT's September 14th notice carries the water board's questions in Section C, developed with the PUC and the board. ERCOT forwards the answers to the board. The transformer is drawn to illustrate.

slides.headline: The request reaches what isn't energized yet
slides.dek: It goes to proposed data centers of 25 to under 75 MW whose load is classified as Substantiated. It also goes to Batch Zero facilities or additions not yet energized at 60 kV or above. The survey goes to operating data centers.

slides.headline: A notarized answer was due October 12th
slides.dek: The developer's own utility files each response. A complete one carries a notarized attestation. A failure to respond is reported to the PUC and the Office of the Governor.

slides.headline: ERCOT expects a report by December 10th
slides.dek: ERCOT says the report will set out conclusions from its own review, with the PUC. A case over a skipped survey is up to local officials, the Tribune reports. A bigger fine needs the Legislature, which meets in Austin in January.

concerns: Caption, carried verbatim: 'Does ERCOT's request reach those 233? No.' is a little stronger than the claims support. c7 covers a Batch Zero 'facility or facility addition' not yet energized, so an operating site's unenergized addition could in principle be reached. Strictly, c4, c7 and c40 support 'the two routes reach different facilities', not a flat No. Left unchanged.

Frame 1 dek: the draft said 'The Texas Tribune's records', which breaks the c27 rule because it makes the records sound like the Tribune's own. It now reads 'Records the Texas Tribune obtained'. 'the state's water use survey' became 'the water board's survey'.

Frame 2 headline: the draft 'One bore for each facility' repeated frame 1's dek and named a topic, not a claim. It is now '101 answered, 233 never did'. 'drawn to illustrate' was missing from the draft, so I added it. The draft sentence 'The order is not which facility' did not read cleanly. It is now 'No bore stands for a named facility.'

Frame 3: the draft dek ran past 34 words and packed two ideas into one sentence. c35 (no known penalty) stays. The local officials point (c34) now sits only on frame 9, which already carries it, so c34 is off frame 3's claim ids. I added c46 because the water board's own page directly states the misdemeanor. 'no authority to prosecute' became 'no authority of its own to prosecute' to match c32.

Frame 5: the draft's '140 of the tank before' read awkwardly. It is now '140 tanks of 10 million gallons'. 140 is figures.tanks_reported and 10 is from c38. The headline names '97 facilities' directly, not 'The 97 that answered'.

Frame 7: I dropped the '0 MW' label. The numeral 0 is not in claims.json or figures.json, so it would fail the numeral gate. If the art needs an end-cap mark, it should go unlabelled. 'plants already running' became 'data centers already operating' to match c40. The headline names 'The request' so the slide makes sense on its own.

Frame 8: the dek no longer fences a phrase with a pair of commas and no longer says 'filed' in the past tense, which implied every response was filed. It now uses the caption's own wording. The 5 p.m. stays in the label.

Frame 9: the headline changed from 'Watch for the report by December 10th' to 'ERCOT expects a report by December 10th', so the slide states it is an expected report (c26). 'local prosecutors' became 'local officials' to match c34, with Tribune attribution. I dropped the PUC co-publication sentence to make room for 'drawn to illustrate'. c25 stays in the claim ids because it defines the report.
